title: Clough Undergraduate Learning Commons
name: Subhajit Bag
text:
"The Swiss Army knife of campus buildings 🔋📚☕"

The Clough Undergraduate Learning Commons—aka CULC—isn’t just a building. It’s the campus hotspot where studying, socializing, and caffeine addiction unite in perfect harmony.

What makes it awesome:

Open 24/7 – You can roll in at 3 a.m. to finish your lab report, cry into your notes, or discover your group project team actually can be productive.

Perfect study vibes – From group pods to quiet corners, there’s a spot for every flavor of academic panic.

The Starbucks downstairs – Because nothing says “academic excellence” like a triple espresso at midnight.

Tech everywhere – Charging outlets for days, huge whiteboards, presentation rooms…basically productivity paradise.

Location – Smack in the middle of campus, so you can “accidentally” bump into friends between classes.

Every time I walk into CULC, I feel like I’m entering the mothership of Georgia Tech—bright, buzzing, and brimming with brilliant people. Whether you’re grinding out code, chatting over coffee, or just people-watching, this place fuels the Yellow Jacket hive mind.

Pro tip: The top floor is underrated—great sunlight, fewer people, and a chance to feel like you’re studying in a glass cloud.

title: Ech Green
name: Subhajit Bag
text:
Tech Green is the heartbeat of Georgia Tech’s campus—a wide, beautiful stretch of green right in the middle of all the action. On any given day, you’ll find students lounging with laptops, playing frisbee, hosting club events, or just soaking up the Atlanta sun between classes. It’s the perfect balance of calm and energy—you can relax here with a coffee, but five minutes later, you might get invited to join a pickup soccer game or watch a pop-up performance.

The view is gorgeous, with the surrounding modern campus buildings framing the lawn, and at night, the soft lighting makes it feel cozy and safe. During spring and fall, it’s the spot for photos, picnics, or just people-watching. In the middle of a busy academic day, Tech Green is a reminder that college life is more than just lectures—it’s a community.

Whether you’re a student, alum, or just visiting campus, grab a snack from nearby food spots, find a sunny patch of grass, and enjoy one of the best gathering spaces Georgia Tech has to offer.

title: John Lewis Student Center
name: Subhajit Bag
text: The John Lewis Student Center at Georgia Tech is one of the best places on campus for both students and visitors. The building is modern, spacious, and full of natural light, making it a comfortable spot to hang out, study, or grab food. The variety of dining options is a big plus—you can find everything from quick snacks to full meals—and the layout makes it easy to settle in with friends or work on group projects. It also hosts plenty of events, so there’s always something happening that adds to the energy of the space. The tribute to John Lewis adds a meaningful touch, reminding everyone of his legacy of leadership and service. It really feels like a hub for campus life.

title: Crosland Tower
name: Subhajit Bag
text: I’ve visited Crosland Tower at Georgia Tech several times lately, and I’m genuinely impressed by how well it balances modern design, thoughtful functionality, and a bit of aesthetic flair. After the renovation, the space feels open and full of natural light, with plenty of study spots ranging from quiet corners to collaborative areas. The specialized studios and labs—like the Innovation and Ideation Studio and Data Visualization Studio—make it more than just a library, and the Crosland Chroma installation on the terrace adds both beauty and safety. Seating capacity has doubled while the building itself became far more energy and water efficient, which is a huge plus. My only small gripe is that the tinted glass panels on the rooftop can sometimes obscure the otherwise amazing views of Midtown and Tech Tower. Still, Crosland Tower has become one of my favorite places on campus to study, reflect, or just enjoy the space—it really feels like a library reimagined for the 21st century.

title: Price Gilbert Memorial Library
name: Sam Dup
text: The ideal location for me to spend my summer break is a place where I can prepare for my certification exam and engage in learning. While I have a private study space in my apartment, I prefer going to the library and staying there until late hours. I find myself more productive in the library environment. However, I'm aware that the library may not have extended hours on Fridays to Sundays. In such cases, I can supplement my study routine by utilizing other resources. Additionally, I enjoy participating in CTF (capture the flag) challenges as they keep me on my toes and allow me to learn from others' experiences through reading their walkthroughs. Although my friends often jokingly complain that I need to "get a life," I find fulfillment in these activities.
